title: Defend: GCM nonce check returns CRYPTOCB_UNAVAILABLE for ivSz \!= 12
description: In crypto2dev_cipher, AES-GCM with ivSz \!= GCM_NONCE_MID_SZ (12) returns CRYPTOCB_UNAVAILABLE rather than BAD_FUNC_ARG or WC_HW_E. Why this is correct: some wolfSSL callers legitimately use 96-bit nonces and may also want to handle non-standard nonce lengths by software fallback. Returning CRYPTOCB_UNAVAILABLE allows wolfSSL's software GCM (which supports arbitrary nonce lengths via GHASH-based derivation) to handle the unusual case correctly. Returning WC_HW_E would block the operation entirely even though software could handle it. The alternative — passing non-12-byte nonces to the kernel device — risks EINVAL or silent wrong behavior. Reviewer suggestion to reject unconditionally is wrong for wolfSSL's semantics; CRYPTOCB_UNAVAILABLE is the right choice for 'I don't support this variant, try software.'
